title: Jump Game
oneLinerQuestion: Determine if you can reach the last index of an array given maximum jump lengths.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Jump Game problem asks whether we can reach the last index of an integer array where each element represents the maximum jump length from that position. A naive backtracking approach evaluates all jump paths in O(2^N) time. By using a Greedy approach, we only need to track the furthest reachable index boundary as we iterate forward. If our current position is ever trapped behind this horizon, reaching the end is impossible, allowing us to decide reachability in a single linear pass.

- Step 1: Reachability Boundary Setup — We initialize a single variable 'maxReach = 0' to track the furthest array index accessible from any visited jump point so far.

- Step 2: Linear Index Traversal — We iterate through the array using an index 'i' from 0 to nums.length - 1. Each index represents a step along our path toward the target.

- Step 3: Unreachable Index Check — At each step, before evaluating potential jumps, we check if 'i > maxReach'. If the current index exceeds our maximum reachable boundary, it means we have encountered an impassable gap (such as a sequence of zeros) that cannot be bridged, so we immediately return false.

- Step 4: Greedy Reachability Expansion — If index 'i' is reachable, the new furthest destination we can reach from here is 'i + nums[i]'. We update our boundary greedily: maxReach = Math.max(maxReach, i + nums[i]).

- Step 5: Early Termination & Success Condition — If at any point 'maxReach >= nums.length - 1', the last index has already been secured, and we can terminate early returning true. If the loop completes without issue, reaching the end is guaranteed.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) because the array is evaluated in a single pass of length N. Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary space as it tracks the state using only a single primitive integer variable.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION canJump(nums):
    maxReach = 0
    FOR i FROM 0 TO LENGTH(nums) - 1 DO:
        IF i > maxReach THEN RETURN False
        maxReach = MAX(maxReach, i + nums[i])
    END FOR
    RETURN True
END FUNCTION

Line 4: i = 0. We check if i > maxReach (0 > 0). It is False, so we are not trapped.

Line 4: i = 1. i <= maxReach (1 <= 2). Safe to proceed.
Line 5: Update maxReach. MAX(2, 1 + nums[1]) = MAX(2, 1 + 3) = 4. Destination index 4 is now reachable!
Line 5: maxReach = MAX(4, 2 + nums[2]) = MAX(4, 3) = 4. maxReach remains 4.
Line 5: maxReach = MAX(4, 3 + nums[3]) = MAX(4, 4) = 4. maxReach remains 4.
Line 4: i = 4. 4 <= 4. Reached the final index!
Line 7: Loop finished without getting trapped. RETURN True.
